description: No clean concept found. It fires mostly late in the game when the player to move is lost or nearly lost, with few legal columns and the opponent holding low threats (a must-block, or a winning cell just above a landing cell). Early in the game it also fires when the opponent has a must-block in column 2 (weaker for column 4, not for column 3). Move order changes it, so it is not a pure board function.
effect: None measurable: steering to max or zero changes move probabilities by at most 0.02 on 4 positions.
notes: 8 dev calls. Best F1 0.237 (p1: no immediate win of my own and every legal move lets the opponent win next turn). The others did worse: lost-position variants 0.14-0.18; late-game plus threats combos 0.185-0.197 (AUROC up to 0.69, sim share ~0.06); column-2 must-block rule 0.12. Minimal pairs show a column-2-specific opponent must-block effect that depends on surrounding stones. Lost positions are also common in the 50-80th percentile band, so the late-game signal is not specific. Possibly a random direction or a mixture.
